transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I came in because... I just feel like I've got this motor running inside me all day long. If I have to sit still for anything—like at church, or out there in the clinic waiting room, or even just at home—I start feeling trapped. I just... I have to get up or do something.

When you feel this motor running inside you and need to move around, do you also notice changes in your mood—like feeling unusually happy, energetic, or irritable—or does your mood feel pretty normal?

No, not really. My mood feels pretty normal, I guess. I don't get... you know, super happy or angry or anything like that. It's just that I can't sit still. It's not really a mood thing, it's just my body needing to move.
How long have you had this feeling of needing to move around? Has it been going on since you were a child, or did it start more recently?

It's been going on since I was a kid, really. Back when I was a boy in school, it was... well, it was exactly the same way. The teachers were always moving my seat around because I just could not stay put. I'd talk out of turn, and I was always getting in trouble for jumping up out of my chair before class was even done. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing for me.
Besides the trouble sitting still, do you find it hard to focus or concentrate on things—like reading, conversations, or tasks at work or home? Do you get distracted easily?

Yeah, I do. Especially with conversations. Like, when folks are talking through ride times, or going over pantry lists, or even church plans... I listen good at first. I really do. But then, I don't know, my mind just slips off. Next thing I know, I realize I missed pieces of what they were saying, pieces I really needed to hear.

You mentioned talking out of turn in school—do you find yourself doing things without thinking them through, or interrupting people when they're talking? Does that still happen to you now as an adult?

Yeah, it definitely still happens. I'll just... jump in with an answer before someone is even done talking. Like with the pastor, or my cousin, or the lady down at the food pantry. I just blurt it out. And then right after, I realize I answered the completely wrong thing, or... or I see that I made them mad by cutting them off. It just slips out before I can catch myself.

Have these difficulties with sitting still, focusing, and blurting things out caused real problems for you—like trouble in school, keeping a job, or maintaining relationships? Or do things generally work out okay for you despite these habits?

Yeah, it... it causes real problems. Things don't really just work out okay for me. People at the church, the folks down at the pantry, and even my own family... they've pretty much stopped trusting me with things. Like doing rides, keeping track of appointments, or handling the supplies. I'll mess it up or get distracted and forget what I was supposed to be doing. I really mean to help them out, I do, but... I just feel like I keep letting everybody down.

You've told me about these difficulties at church, at the food pantry, and at home. Are there any situations or times—maybe certain activities or places—where you find you can sit still and focus pretty well, or does this restlessness and trouble focusing happen pretty much everywhere, all the time?

I don't really know if there's a time where it stops. It just feels like it's all the time. Everywhere I go, whether I'm at the church, the pantry, or just sitting at home... I just can't sit still or keep my mind on one thing. It's just always there.

You mentioned these difficulties happen pretty much all the time. But I want to ask: have there ever been any weeks or months in your life—maybe during a particular job, or a specific time period—where you noticed you could sit still better, or your mind stayed focused more easily than it usually does?

No, I can't really think of any time like that. I mean, I try to think back... but it's never really stopped or gotten better, not even for a few weeks. It's just always been this way. I don't remember any time in my life where my mind just stayed focused, or where I could sit still without it being a struggle. It's pretty much just a constant thing.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with lifelong symptoms of hyperactivity-impulsivity and inattention beginning in childhood, persisting into adulthood across multiple settings (school, church, food pantry, home). Core ADHD symptoms include: inability to sit still ('motor running inside'), difficulty sustaining attention in conversations, impulsive interruptions/blurting out answers prematurely, and chronic functional impairment in social relationships and community roles. No mood elevation, irritability episodes, or conduct disorder features are present. The pervasive, cross-situational, and longitudinal nature of symptoms without remission periods supports ADHD diagnosis rather than other conditions.
